categories.name: Overall aesthetic
categories.summary: A dark, archival internet-horror documentary. Most of the running time is web pages, comments and photos laid out as tilted 3D sheets on a dark ground, cut against long stretches of raw source footage. Graphics are desaturated and grainy; raw footage keeps its own colour and age. In the 5 references, motion graphics make up 45-80% of the clips.

rules.text: Show evidence as the thing itself: the real web page, comment, file name or broadcast, in 3D on a dark ground, never a re-typed version.

categories.name: Mood and emotion
categories.summary: Horror, built from restraint rather than shocks: dark pages that drift, a calm narrator, and moments where the narration stops so the real footage or audio plays on its own. Dread comes from the evidence being real and the viewer being made to look closely at it.

categories.summary: Near-black grounds, desaturated pages and two accent colours. Treated shots measure 14-19% saturation against 20-42% for raw footage, with a neutral tint. categories.name: Camera movement
categories.summary: Every graphic moves (rule 7). Push-ins dominate: in a 60 s sample, 64% of all shots moved (raw footage included) and 77% of the moves were zoom-ins. categories.name: Editing rhythm
categories.summary: A block is a run of shots with one look (for example, all tilted-page shots), ending when the look changes. Expect 4-6 blocks per minute. Graphic blocks run 8-11 s; raw-footage blocks run 11-16 s and up to 27 s; title cards 2-4 s. Inside a block the picture keeps changing, so the cut still feels quick (the 60 s sample averaged 1.4 s per shot).

rules.text: Hold graphic blocks 8-11 s and raw-footage blocks 11-16 s; let a raw moment run to 25 s or more when it is the evidence.

categories.name: Music and sound
categories.summary: Narration leads. Loudness is measured in LUFS (the average loudness of the whole mix on a loudness meter): the references sit at -17.6 to -14.4 LUFS, 4 of the 5 near -17. The voice is calm, 155-195 words per minute, with 4-8 pauses of 0.6 s or more per minute (median 0.8 s). Music is a low bed (8.4 dB under the voice in the 60 s sample). Raw clips bring their own sound, faded by rule 8.

rules.text: Master to -17 LUFS integrated; keep the voice clear and steady.
Keep music 8 dB under the narration on the loudness meter, as a dark ambient bed, not a melody.
Let the raw footage's own sound play when it is the evidence, with the narration silent.

categories.name: Storytelling
categories.summary: An investigation told in order of discovery: a cold open on the most disturbing material, the host on camera to set up the question, then the evidence trail (searches, archived pages, comments, broadcasts) one step at a time, chapter titles at each turn, and a sign-off with credits. The host returns on camera at chapter turns.

rulebook.text: Mood is horror, always. Every picture, text, movement and sound adds dread or unease. Nothing bright, cute or playful unless it is glitched, desaturated or distorted so it feels wrong.
All text you add uses the VCR OSD Mono font: titles, dates, labels, captions, chapter cards. No second font. Captured pages, posts and broadcasts keep their own fonts.

Between shots, either cut straight or use one of four transitions: crossfade, dip to black, VHS (tape start, rewind, tracking, static) or glitch. A light leak counts as a crossfade. No wipes, slides, spins, zoom transitions or shape reveals.
Shot size is mostly medium. Use close-up or extreme close-up only to point at a detail (a face, a word, a figure in the frame).
Compose to the centre: the subject, title or key line sits on the centre of the frame.

High contrast, dark grade, vintage texture. Treated shots sit at a median brightness of 70-90 on a 0-255 scale. Before the first edit, pick 3-5 texture types for the video (film grain, VHS noise and tracking lines, CRT scanlines and curvature, dust and scratches, light leak), list them in the edit notes, and put at least one on every treated shot.
Every graphic shot moves: pan, zoom or push, tracking, 3D tilt, or wide angle, sometimes with lens distortion. No still graphics.

Raw clip audio: start the audio 2.0 s before its picture cut (pre-roll; less if the source has no 2.0 s of head) and end it with the picture. Fade in over the first 6.44 s and out over the last 2.74 s. If the audio clip is shorter than 9.18 s, multiply both fade lengths by (clip length / 9.18) x 0.98.
Crossfade inside a montage. Dip to black between sections (a new date, place or time period). Mark a chapter change with VHS (tape start, rewind or static).
